title: Why alloys are harder
caption: In a pure metal the layers of identical atoms slide over each other easily. Larger atoms of a second metal (here tin in copper, making bronze) distort the layers, so they cannot slide as easily and the alloy is harder.
alt: Left: a regular lattice of copper atoms. Right: the same lattice with a few larger tin atoms disrupting the rows.
description: Pure copper: regular rows that slide easily.
Bronze: larger tin atoms among the copper, distorting the rows.
